why: With positive entries, if every k x k square fits the threshold then every smaller square does too (a smaller square sits inside a larger one), so validity is monotone in k. Binary-search k, and check a given k in O(n^2) using a 2-D prefix-sum table for O(1) square sums.
hints: If all 3x3 squares are within the threshold, what can you say about all 2x2 squares? Positive values make the answer monotone.
Build pre[i][j] = sum of the top-left i x j block; any k x k square sum is pre[i+k][j+k] - pre[i][j+k] - pre[i+k][j] + pre[i][j].
Binary-search k in [1, n]; for each mid scan all squares and fail fast on the first sum above threshold. O(n^2 log n).
pitfalls: The condition is that EVERY k x k square fits, so check the maximum square sum, not the minimum.
Return 0 when even a single cell exceeds the threshold.
Get the inclusion-exclusion signs right; an off-by-one in prefix indices silently shifts squares.
